cards.title: Running Between the Hills of al-Safa and al-Marwah in Pilgrimage
cards.note: Surah 2:158 reassures believers that there is no blame in pacing between al-Safa and al-Marwah, incorporating a pre-Islamic Arabian pilgrimage rite in which tribes ran between the two hills for the idols Manat, Isaf, and Na'ilah.

discussion.view: Muslim tradition holds that running between al-Safa and al-Marwah originated with Hagar's search for water for Ishmael, and that pre-Islamic Arabs later placed pagan idols on the two hills before Islam restored the Abrahamic rite.
discussion.reply: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1643, 4496, and Sahih Muslim 1277, Companions including Anas ibn Malik and the Ansar describe pacing between al-Safa and al-Marwah as a pre-Islamic custom performed for the idol Manat or the coastal idols Isaf and Na'ilah. Those reports record that early converts hesitated to perform the circuit because they recognized it as a pre-Islamic polytheistic ceremony.

cards.quranEn: Surely al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God. Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he goes around both of them. And whoever does good voluntarily – surely God is thankful, knowing.
quranHighlights: Surely al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God
(there is) no blame on him if he goes around both of them

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari (A'ishah and Anas on Pre-Islamic Rite at al-Safa and al-Marwah)
sources.workSub: Sahih al-Bukhari (A'ishah and Anas on Pre-Islamic Rite at al-Safa and al-Marwah)
sources.en: But in fact, this divine inspiration was revealed concerning the Ansar who used to assume Ihram for worshipping an idol called "Manat" which they used to worship at a place called Al-Mushallal before they embraced Islam, and whoever assumed Ihram (for the idol), would consider it not right to perform Tawaf between Safa and Marwa. When they embraced Islam, they asked Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) regarding it, saying, "O Allah's Apostle! We used to refrain from Tawaf between Safa and Marwa." So Allah revealed: 'Verily; (the mountains) As-Safa and Al-Marwa are among the symbols of Allah.' " Aisha added, "Surely, Allah's Apostle set the tradition of Tawaf between Safa and Marwa, so nobody is allowed to omit the Tawaf between them."
highlights: worshipping an idol called "Manat"
We used to refrain from Tawaf between Safa and Marwa
sources.orig: وَلَكِنَّهَا أُنْزِلَتْ فِي الأَنْصَارِ، كَانُوا قَبْلَ أَنْ يُسْلِمُوا يُهِلُّونَ لِمَنَاةَ الطَّاغِيَةِ الَّتِي كَانُوا يَعْبُدُونَهَا عِنْدَ الْمُشَلَّلِ، فَكَانَ مَنْ أَهَلَّ يَتَحَرَّجُ أَنْ يَطُوفَ بِالصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمُوا سَأَلُوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ ذَلِكَ قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّا كُنَّا نَتَحَرَّجُ أَنْ نَطُوفَ بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏{‏إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ‏}‏ الآيَةَ‏.‏ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ ـ رضى الله عنها ـ وَقَدْ سَنَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الطَّوَافَ بَيْنَهُمَا، فَلَيْسَ لأَحَدٍ أَنْ يَتْرُكَ الطَّوَافَ بَيْنَهُمَا‏.‏

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari (Anas ibn Malik on Safa and Marwah as a Pre-Islamic Custom)
sources.workSub: Sahih al-Bukhari (Anas ibn Malik on Safa and Marwah as a Pre-Islamic Custom)
sources.en: Narrated `Asim bin Sulaiman:I asked Anas bin Malik about Safa and Marwa. Anas replied, "We used to consider (i.e. going around) them a custom of the Pre-islamic period of Ignorance, so when Islam came, we gave up going around them. Then Allah revealed" "Verily, Safa and Marwa (i.e. two mountains at Mecca) are among the Symbols of Allah.
highlights: We used to consider (i.e. going around) them a custom of the Pre-islamic period of Ignorance
sources.orig: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ، قَالَ سَأَلْتُ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ الصَّفَا، وَالْمَرْوَةِ،‏.‏ فَقَالَ كُنَّا نَرَى أَنَّهُمَا مِنْ أَمْرِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الإِسْلاَمُ أَمْسَكْنَا عَنْهُمَا، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏{‏إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا‏}‏‏.‏

sources.title: Sahih Muslim (A'ishah on Pre-Islamic Pilgrims Assuming Ihram for Manat)
sources.workSub: Sahih Muslim (A'ishah on Pre-Islamic Pilgrims Assuming Ihram for Manat)
sources.en: Do you know in what context (this verse was revealed)? (It was revealed in this context) that the Ansar in the Days of Ignorance pronounced the Talbiya for two idols. (fixedl on the bank of the river which were called Isaf and Na'ila. The people went there, and then circumambulated between al-Safa' and al-Marwa and then got their heads shaved. With the advent of Islam they (the Muslims) did not like to circumambulate between them as they used to do during the Days of Ignorance. It was on account of this that Allah. the Exalted and Majestic, revealed:" Verily al-Safe and al-Marwa are among the Signs of Allah" to the end of the verse.
highlights: pronounced the Talbiya for two idols
circumambulated between al-Safa' and al-Marwa
sources.orig: وَهَلْ تَدْرِي فِيمَا كَانَ ذَاكَ إِنَّمَا كَانَ ذَاكَ أَنَّ الأَنْصَارَ كَانُوا يُهِلُّونَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ لِصَنَمَيْنِ عَلَى شَطِّ الْبَحْرِ يُقَالُ لَهُمَا إِسَافٌ وَنَائِلَةٌ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ يَجِيئُونَ فَيَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ ثُمَّ يَحْلِقُونَ ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا جَاءَ الإِسْلاَمُ كَرِهُوا أَنْ يَطُوفُوا بَيْنَهُمَا لِلَّذِي كَانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ قَالَتْ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ‏ {‏ إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ‏}‏ إِلَى آخِرِهَا - قَالَتْ - فَطَافُوا ‏.‏

cards.quranAr: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ

cards.title: Pouring Forth from 'Arafat and Reforming the Pre-Islamic Quraysh Hums Rite
cards.note: Surah 2:199 commands Quraysh to 'press on from where the people press on' at 'Arafat, reforming the pre-Islamic Hums privilege whereby Quraysh halted at Muzdalifah while other Arabs stood at 'Arafat.

discussion.view: Classical exegetes state that Abraham originally stood at 'Arafat, and that the Quraysh later innovated the Hums privilege of remaining inside the sanctuary border at Muzdalifah until Surah 2:199 restored Abraham's station.
discussion.reply: Hadith reports in Sahih al-Bukhari 4520 and Tafsir al-Tabari on 2:199 document that both the station at 'Arafat and the rushing procession (ifadah) through Muzdalifah were established pre-Islamic Arabian pilgrimage ceremonies. Surah 2:199 unified the two pre-Islamic tribal itineraries by requiring the Meccan Hums to join the wider Arab pilgrim assembly at 'Arafat.

cards.quranEn: Then press on from where the people press on, and ask forgiveness from God. Surely God is forgiving, compassionate.
quranHighlights: Then press on from where the people press on

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari ('A'ishah on Pre-Islamic Quraysh Hums Stopping at Muzdalifah)
sources.workSub: Sahih al-Bukhari ('A'ishah on Pre-Islamic Quraysh Hums Stopping at Muzdalifah)
sources.en: Narrated `Aisha:The Quraish people and those who embraced their religion, used to stay at Muzdalifa and used to call themselves Al-Hums, while the rest of the Arabs used to stay at `Arafat.
highlights: used to stay at Muzdalifa and used to call themselves Al-Hums, while the rest of the Arabs used to stay at `Arafat
sources.orig: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ خَازِمٍ، حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ ـ رضى الله عنها ـ كَانَتْ قُرَيْشٌ وَمَنْ دَانَ دِينَهَا يَقِفُونَ بِالْمُزْدَلِفَةِ، وَكَانُوا يُسَمَّوْنَ الْحُمْسَ، وَكَانَ سَائِرُ الْعَرَبِ يَقِفُونَ بِعَرَفَاتٍ، فَلَمَّا جَاءَ الإِسْلاَمُ أَمَرَ اللَّهُ نَبِيَّهُ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ يَأْتِيَ عَرَفَاتٍ، ثُمَّ يَقِفَ بِهَا ثُمَّ يُفِيضَ مِنْهَا، فَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى ‏{‏ثُمَّ أَفِيضُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ النَّاسُ‏}‏

sources.title: Tafsir al-Tabari ('A'ishah on Quraysh Al-Hums and Quran 2:199)
sources.workSub: Tafsir al-Tabari ('A'ishah on Quraysh Al-Hums and Quran 2:199)
sources.en: The Quraysh and those who followed their religion - and they were Al-Hums - used to stand at Al-Muzdalifah saying, "We are the dwellers of Allah!" while those other than them used to stand at 'Arafah. Thus Allah revealed: {Then press on from where the people press on}.
highlights: used to stand at Al-Muzdalifah
while those other than them used to stand at 'Arafah
Then press on from where the people press on
sources.orig: عن عائشة قالت: كانت قريش ومن كان على دينها -وهم الحمس- يقفون بالمزدلفة يقولون: " نحن قطين الله!"، وكان من سواهم يقفون بعرفة. فأنـزل الله: " ثم أفيضوا من حيث أفاض الناس "

cards.quranAr: ثُمَّ أَفِيضُواْ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ أَفَاضَ ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ

cards.title: Twelve Lunar Months, Four Sacred Months, and Banning Intercalation (al-Nasi')
cards.note: Surah 9:36–37 fixes the year at twelve lunar months with four sacred truce months and abolishes pre-Islamic Arabian calendar postponement (al-nasi'), which shifted sacred status between Muharram and Safar as recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari 4406 and al-Tabari.

discussion.view: Islamic tradition holds that God ordained twelve lunar months and four sacred truce months at creation for Abraham's sanctuary, and that pagan Kinanah calendar-keepers corrupted this order through postponement (al-nasi').
discussion.reply: Sahih al-Bukhari 4406 and Tafsir al-Tabari on 9:37 confirm that the four sacred truce months—Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab Mudar—together with the intercalary office of Junadah ibn 'Awf (Abu Thumamah) of Kinanah were institutions of pre-Islamic Arabian tribal law designed to synchronize seasonal trade and pilgrimage fairs.

cards.quranEn: [36] Surely the number of months with God is twelve, (written) in the Book of God on the day when He created the heavens and the earth. Of them, four are sacred. That is the right religion. Do not do yourselves evil during them, but fight (against) the idolaters all together, as they fight you all together, and know that God is with the ones who guard (themselves). [37] The postponement is an increase of disbelief by which those who disbelieve go astray. They make it profane (one) year, and make it sacred (another) year, to adjust the number (of months) God has made sacred, and to profane what God has made sacred. The evil of their deeds is made to appear enticing to them, but God does not guide the people who are disbelievers.
quranHighlights: Surely the number of months with God is twelve
The postponement is an increase of disbelief
They make it profane (one) year, and make it sacred (another) year

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari (Abu Bakrah on the Twelve Months and Four Sacred Months)
sources.workSub: Sahih al-Bukhari (Abu Bakrah on the Twelve Months and Four Sacred Months)
sources.en: Narrated Abu Bakra:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Time has taken its original shape which it had when Allah created the Heavens and the Earth. The year is of twelve months, four of which are sacred, and out of these (four) three are in succession, i.e. Dhul-Qa'da, Dhul-Hijja and Al-Muharram, and the fourth is Rajab which is named after the Mudar tribe, between (the month of) Jumaida (ath-thania) and Sha'ban."
highlights: The year is of twelve months, four of which are sacred, and out of these (four) three are in succession, i.e. Dhul-Qa'da, Dhul-Hijja and Al-Muharram, and the fourth is Rajab which is named after the Mudar tribe
sources.orig: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَهَّابِ، حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي بَكْرَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ الزَّمَانُ قَدِ اسْتَدَارَ كَهَيْئَةِ يَوْمَ خَلَقَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضَ، السَّنَةُ اثْنَا عَشَرَ شَهْرًا مِنْهَا أَرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ ثَلاَثَةٌ مُتَوَالِيَاتٌ ذُو الْقَعْدَةِ وَذُو الْحِجَّةِ وَالْمُحَرَّمُ، وَرَجَبُ مُضَرَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ جُمَادَى وَشَعْبَانَ، أَىُّ شَهْرٍ هَذَا ‏"‏ قُلْنَا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ‏.‏

sources.title: Tafsir al-Tabari
sources.en: "'The postponement' (Al-Nasi') is that 'Junadah bin 'Awf bin Umayyah Al-Kinani' used to arrive at the season (of Hajj) every year, and his patronymic was 'Abu Thumamah', so he would call out: 'Verily, Abu Thumamah is neither opposed nor faulted. Verily, Safar of the first year is profane this year,' so he makes it profane for the people. Thus he makes Safar sacred one year, and makes Al-Muharram sacred one year. And that is His saying, Exalted is He: {The postponement is an increase of disbelief} until His saying: {the disbelievers}. And His saying: {The postponement is an increase of disbelief}, He says: they leave Al-Muharram (profane) one year, and one year they make it sacred."
highlights: 'The postponement' (Al-Nasi')
Thus he makes Safar sacred one year, and makes Al-Muharram sacred one year
sources.orig: " النسيء "، هو أن " جُنَادة بن عوف بن أمية الكناني"، كان يوافي الموسم كلَّ عام, وكان يُكنى " أبا ثُمَامة ", (5) فينادي: " ألا إنّ أبا ثمامة لا يُحَابُ ولا يُعَابُ, (6) ألا وإن صَفَر العامِ الأوَّلِ العامَ حلالٌ"، (7) فيحله الناس, فيحرم صَفَر عامًا, ويحرِّم المحرم عامًا, فذلك قوله تعالى: (إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر)، إلى قوله: (الكافرين). وقوله: (إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر)، يقول: يتركون المحرم عامًا, وعامًا يحرِّمونه.

cards.quranAr: إِنَّ عِدَّةَ ٱلشُّهُورِ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱثۡنَا عَشَرَ شَهۡرٗا فِي كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ يَوۡمَ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ مِنۡهَآ أَرۡبَعَةٌ حُرُمٞۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُۚ فَلَا تَظۡلِمُواْ فِيهِنَّ أَنفُسَكُمۡۚ وَقَٰتِلُواْ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ كَآفَّةٗ كَمَا يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمۡ كَآفَّةٗۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ ﴿36﴾ إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّسِيٓءُ زِيَادَةٞ فِي ٱلۡكُفۡرِۖ يُضَلُّ بِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُحِلُّونَهُۥ عَامٗا وَيُحَرِّمُونَهُۥ عَامٗا لِّيُوَاطِـُٔواْ عِدَّةَ مَا حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ فَيُحِلُّواْ مَا حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُۚ زُيِّنَ لَهُمۡ سُوٓءُ أَعۡمَٰلِهِمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ ﴿37﴾

cards.title: Pre-Islamic Pilgrimage Taboo of Entering Houses from Their Backs
cards.note: Surah 2:189 declares that 'it is not piety to come to your houses from their backs, but come to your houses by their doors,' abolishing the pre-Islamic Arabian taboo in which pilgrims in Ihram climbed into their homes from behind.

discussion.view: Commentators explain that Surah 2:189 abolished a pre-Islamic superstition added by Arabian tribes to the Abrahamic pilgrimage, teaching that true piety lies in reverence toward God rather than ritual taboos.
discussion.reply: Sahih al-Bukhari 1803 and 4512 and Tafsir al-Tabari on 2:189 record that the Ansar and non-Hums Arabs observed the state of ritual consecration (ihram) before Islam by refusing to pass under door lintels, whereas Qurayshi Hums exempted themselves. The verse presupposes and directly legislates within this local Hijazi tribal distinction between Hums and non-Hums pilgrims.

cards.quranEn: They ask you about the new moons. Say: ‘They are appointed times for the people, and for the pilgrimage.’ It is not piety to come to (your) houses from their backs, but (true) piety (belongs to) the one who guards (himself). Come to (your) houses by their doors, and guard (yourselves) against God, so that you may prosper.
quranHighlights: It is not piety to come to (your) houses from their backs
Come to (your) houses by their doors

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari (Al-Bara' on Pre-Islamic Pilgrims Entering Houses from Behind)
sources.workSub: Sahih al-Bukhari (Al-Bara' on Pre-Islamic Pilgrims Entering Houses from Behind)
sources.en: Narrated Abu 'Is-haq:I heard Al-Bara' saying, "The above Verse was revealed regarding us, for the Ansar on returning from Hajj never entered their houses through the proper doors but from behind. One of the Ansar came and entered through the door and he was taunted for it.
highlights: the Ansar on returning from Hajj never entered their houses through the proper doors but from behind
sources.orig: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْوَلِيدِ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ الْبَرَاءَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ يَقُولُ نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ فِينَا، كَانَتِ الأَنْصَارُ إِذَا حَجُّوا فَجَاءُوا لَمْ يَدْخُلُوا مِنْ قِبَلِ أَبْوَابِ بُيُوتِهِمْ، وَلَكِنْ مِنْ ظُهُورِهَا، فَجَاءَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ، فَدَخَلَ مِنْ قِبَلِ بَابِهِ، فَكَأَنَّهُ عُيِّرَ بِذَلِكَ، فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهَا وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنِ اتَّقَى وَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا‏}‏‏.‏

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari (Pre-Islamic Ihram Custom of Entering Houses from the Back)
sources.workSub: Sahih al-Bukhari (Pre-Islamic Ihram Custom of Entering Houses from the Back)
sources.en: Narrated Al-Bara:In the Pre-Islamic Period when the people assumed Ihram, they would enter their houses from the back.
highlights: when the people assumed Ihram, they would enter their houses from the back
sources.orig: حَدَّثَنَا عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُوسَى، عَنْ إِسْرَائِيلَ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ، قَالَ كَانُوا إِذَا أَحْرَمُوا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ أَتَوُا الْبَيْتَ مِنْ ظَهْرِهِ، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهَا وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنِ اتَّقَى وَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا‏}‏

sources.title: Tafsir al-Tabari (Al-Bara' on Pre-Islamic Pilgrims Entering Houses from Behind)
sources.workSub: Tafsir al-Tabari (Al-Bara' on Pre-Islamic Pilgrims Entering Houses from Behind)
sources.en: I heard al-Bara' say: The Ansar, when they performed Hajj and returned, would not enter the houses except from their backs. He said: Then a man from the Ansar came and entered from his door, and he was questioned about that. Thus, this verse was revealed: {It is not piety to come to (your) houses from their backs} (96).
highlights: when they performed Hajj and returned, would not enter the houses except from their backs
sources.orig: سمعت البراء يقول: كانت الأنصار إذا حَجوا ورَجعوا لم يدخلوا البيوت إلا من ظُهورها. قال: فجاء رجل من الأنصار فدخل من بابه، فقيل له في ذلك، فنـزلت هذه الآية: " وليسَ البرُّ بأن تأتوا البيوت من ظهورها " (96) .

cards.quranAr: ۞يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡأَهِلَّةِۖ قُلۡ هِيَ مَوَٰقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَلَيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرُّ بِأَن تَأۡتُواْ ٱلۡبُيُوتَ مِن ظُهُورِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰۗ وَأۡتُواْ ٱلۡبُيُوتَ مِنۡ أَبۡوَٰبِهَاۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ

cards.title: Abolishing Pre-Islamic Dedicated Camels: Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasilah, and Ham
cards.note: Surah 5:103 abolishes four pre-Islamic Arabian classes of livestock consecrated to idols—Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasilah, and Ham—defined in detail by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab in Sahih al-Bukhari 4623 and Tafsir Ibn Kathir on 5:103.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators cite Surah 5:103 and the Prophetic report on 'Amr ibn Luhayy al-Khuza'i to show that consecrating slit-eared or free-roaming camels to idols was a polytheistic innovation rejected by Islam.
discussion.reply: Sahih al-Bukhari 4623 and Tafsir Ibn Kathir on 5:103 preserve Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab's technical legal taxonomy of four Hijazi livestock categories—Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasilah, and Ham—whose milk, offspring, and backs were tabooed for local deities. The verse's four technical terms are drawn directly from pre-Islamic Arabian pastoral and sanctuary law.

cards.quranEn: God has not appointed any baḥ īra or sā’iba or waṣīla or ḥ āmi, but those who disbelieve forge lies against God. Most of them do not understand.
quranHighlights: God has not appointed any baḥ īra or sā’iba or waṣīla or ḥ āmi

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4623 (Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: Definitions of Bahirah and Sa'ibah)
sources.en: Bahira is a she-camel whose milk is kept for the idols and nobody is allowed to milk it; Sa'iba was the she-camel which they used to set free for their gods and nothing was allowed to be carried on it.
highlights: Bahira is a she-camel whose milk is kept for the idols
Sa'iba was the she-camel which they used to set free for their gods
sources.orig: الْبَحِيرَةُ الَّتِي يُمْنَعُ دَرُّهَا لِلطَّوَاغِيتِ فَلاَ يَحْلُبُهَا أَحَدٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ‏.‏ وَالسَّائِبَةُ كَانُوا يُسَيِّبُونَهَا لآلِهَتِهِمْ لاَ يُحْمَلُ عَلَيْهَا شَىْءٌ‏.‏

sources.title: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab on Wasilah and Ham in Sahih al-Bukhari)
sources.workSub: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab on Wasilah and Ham in Sahih al-Bukhari)
sources.en: As for the Wasilah, it is a female camel setting the first delivery as a female, then giving birth to another female at its second delivery. They used to set them free for their idols, if she connected one to the other without a male between them. As for the Ham, it is a male camel which copulates a set number of copulations, and when he finished his copulations they would leave him for the idols, exempt him from carrying burdens, so nothing would be carried on him, and they called him a Hami."
highlights: As for the Wasilah, it is a female camel
As for the Ham, it is a male camel
leave him for the idols, exempt him from carrying burdens
sources.orig: و " الوصيلة " : الناقة البكر ، تبكر في أول نتاج الإبل ، ثم تثني بعد بأنثى ، وكانوا يسيبونها لطواغيتهم ، إن وصلت إحداهما بالأخرى ليس بينهما ذكر . و " الحام " : فحل الإبل يضرب الضراب المعدود ، فإذا قضى ضرابه ودعوه للطواغيت ، وأعفوه عن الحمل ، فلم يحمل عليه شيء ، وسموه الحامي .

cards.quranAr: مَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنۢ بَحِيرَةٖ وَلَا سَآئِبَةٖ وَلَا وَصِيلَةٖ وَلَا حَامٖ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَۖ وَأَكۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ

cards.title: Outlawing Pre-Islamic Naked Tawaf: 'Take Your Adornment at Every Mosque'
cards.note: Surah 7:31–32 commands 'Sons of Adam, take your adornment in every mosque,' abolishing the pre-Islamic Hums custom requiring non-Qurayshi pilgrims to circumambulate the Kaaba naked unless lent Hums garments.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes explain that pagan Quraysh forced outside tribes to either rent Hums clothing or circle the Kaaba naked, and that Surah 7:31 restored modest dress to the Abrahamic sanctuary.
discussion.reply: Sahih Muslim 3028 and 1219 and Tafsir al-Tabari on 7:31 preserve the pre-Islamic ritual poetry recited by naked pilgrims circling the Meccan sanctuary. While ending the nudity taboo, Islamic pilgrimage law retained the underlying Meccan circumambulation (tawaf) and the requirement to shed ordinary stitched clothing for special sanctuary garments.

cards.quranEn: [31] Sons of Adam! Take your adornment in every mosque, and eat and drink, but do not act wantonly. Surely He does not love the wanton. [32] Say: ‘Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of (His) provision?’ Say: ‘It is exclusively for those who have believed in this present life on the Day of Resurrection.’ In this way We make the signs distinct for a people who know.
quranHighlights: Sons of Adam! Take your adornment in every mosque
Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants

sources.title: Sahih Muslim
sources.en: Ibn Abbas reported:During the pre-Islamic days women circumambulated the Ka'ba nakedly, and said: Who would provide cloth to cover the one who is circumambulating the Ka'ba so that she would cover her private parts? And then she would say: Today will be exposed the whole or the part and what is exposed I shall not make it lawful. It was in this connection that the verse was revealed:" Adorn yourself at every place of worship" (vii)
highlights: During the pre-Islamic days women circumambulated the Ka'ba nakedly
Adorn yourself at every place of worship
sources.orig: ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ كَانَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ تَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ وَهِيَ عُرْيَانَةٌ فَتَقُولُ مَنْ يُعِيرُنِي تِطْوَافًا تَجْعَلُهُ عَلَى فَرْجِهَا وَتَقُولُ الْيَوْمَ يَبْدُو بَعْضُهُ أَوْ كُلُّهُ فَمَا بَدَا مِنْهُ فَلاَ أُحِلُّهُ فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ ‏{‏ خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ‏}‏

sources.title: Sahih Muslim
sources.en: Hisham narrated on the authority of his father that the Arabs with the exception of Hums who were Quraish, and their descendants, circumambulated the House naked. They kept circumambulating In this state of nudity unless the Hums supplied to them the clothes. The male provided (clothes) to the male and the female provided clothes to the female.
highlights: the Arabs with the exception of Hums who were Quraish, and their descendants, circumambulated the House naked
unless the Hums supplied to them the clothes
sources.orig: قَالَ كَانَتِ الْعَرَبُ تَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ عُرَاةً إِلاَّ الْحُمْسَ وَالْحُمْسُ قُرَيْشٌ وَمَا وَلَدَتْ كَانُوا يَطُوفُونَ عُرَاةً إِلاَّ أَنْ تُعْطِيَهُمُ الْحُمْسُ ثِيَابًا فَيُعْطِي الرِّجَالُ الرِّجَالَ وَالنِّسَاءُ النِّسَاءَ

sources.title: Tafsir al-Tabari
sources.en: That women used to perform Tawaf around the House while naked = and he said in another place: without clothes = except that a woman would place a piece of cloth over her private parts, in what was described, God willing, and she would say: "Today, a part or all of it will be unveiled, But whatever is exposed of it, I do not allow." He said: Then this verse was revealed: {Take your adornment in every mosque}.
highlights: women used to perform Tawaf around the House while naked
Take your adornment in every mosque
sources.orig: عن ابن عباس: أن النساء كنّ يطفن بالبيت عراة = وقال في موضع آخر: بغير ثياب = إلا أن تجعل المرأة على فرجها خِرقة، فيما وُصِف إن شاء الله, وتقول: الْيَــوْمَ يَبْــدُو بَعْضُــهُ أَوْ كُلُّــهُ فَمَــا بَــدَا مِنْــهُ فَــلا أُحِلُّــهُ قال: فنـزلت هذه الآية: (خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد).

cards.quranAr: ۞يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ خُذُواْ زِينَتَكُمۡ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسۡجِدٖ وَكُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ وَلَا تُسۡرِفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُسۡرِفِينَ ﴿31﴾ قُلۡ مَنۡ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزۡقِۚ قُلۡ هِيَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا خَالِصَةٗ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمٖ يَعۡلَمُونَ ﴿32﴾

cards.title: Ban on Wine (Khamr), Arrow-Gambling (Maysir), and Sacrificial Stones
cards.note: Surah 5:90–91 bans wine, maysir arrow-gambling, ansab sacrificial stones, and azlam divination arrows, targeting the pre-Islamic pairing of wine and arrow-lots in 'Antarah's Mu'allaqah, the Kaaba azlam in Bukhari 1601, and ansab in Ibn Kathir.

discussion.view: Classical commentators note that God prohibited wine and gambling in stages before issuing the final categorical ban in Surah 5:90–91 alongside pagan sacrificial stones and divination arrows.
discussion.reply: Pre-Islamic poetry, including verse 54 of the Mu'allaqah of 'Antarah ibn Shaddad (~AD 580), pairs wine-purchasing with maysir arrow-casting over slaughtered camels as twin marks of Arabian chivalry, while Sahih al-Bukhari 1601 and Tafsir Ibn Kathir on 5:90 document the sacrificial stone altars (ansab) and divination arrows (azlam) used in pre-Islamic sanctuaries.

cards.quranEn: [90] You who believe! Wine, games of chance, stones, and divination arrows are an abomination, part of the work of Satan. So avoid it in order that you may prosper. [91] Satan only wishes to cause enmity and hatred among you with wine and games of chance, and to keep you from the remembrance of God and from the prayer. Will you refrain?
quranHighlights: Wine, games of chance, stones, and divination arrows are an abomination

sources.title: Mu'allaqah of 'Antarah ibn Shaddad
sources.ref: Mu'allaqah of 'Antarah, v. 54 (Pre-Islamic Wine-Drinking and Maysir Arrow-Lots)
sources.en: Whose hands were brisk in casting lots, when winter demands such recreation: a man censured for his disregard of wealth, and for causing the wine-merchant to strike his flag, by purchasing all his store .
highlights: Whose hands were brisk in casting lots
causing the wine-merchant to strike his flag, by purchasing all his store

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1601 (Pre-Islamic Divination Arrows [Azlam] in the Ka'ba)
sources.en: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came to Mecca, he refused to enter the Ka`ba with idols in it. He ordered (idols to be taken out). So they were taken out. The people took out the pictures of Abraham and Ishmael holding Azlams in their hands. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "May Allah curse these people. By Allah, both Abraham and Ishmael never did the game of chance with Azlams."
highlights: holding Azlams in their hands
the game of chance with Azlams
sources.orig: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَعْمَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ، حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ، حَدَّثَنَا عِكْرِمَةُ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَمَّا قَدِمَ أَبَى أَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْبَيْتَ وَفِيهِ الآلِهَةُ فَأَمَرَ بِهَا فَأُخْرِجَتْ فَأَخْرَجُوا صُورَةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمَا الأَزْلاَمُ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ قَاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَمَا وَاللَّهِ قَدْ عَلِمُوا أَنَّهُمَا لَمْ يَسْتَقْسِمَا بِهَا قَطُّ ‏"‏‏.‏

sources.title: Tafsir Ibn Kathir
sources.ref: Ibn Kathir on Quran 5:90 (Pre-Islamic Sacrificial Stones [Ansab] and Divination Arrows [Azlam])
sources.en: As for Al-Ansab, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, and others said: "They were stone altars near which they would slaughter their sacrifices." As for Al-Azlam, they also said: "They were arrows that they used for lotteries to make decisions."
highlights: They were stone altars near which they would slaughter their sacrifices
They were arrows that they used for lotteries to make decisions
sources.orig: وأما الأنصاب ، فقال ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء وسعيد بن جبير والحسن ، وغير واحد : هي حجارة كانوا يذبحون قرابينهم عندها . وأما الأزلام فقالوا أيضا : هي قداح كانوا يستقسمون بها .

cards.quranAr: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡخَمۡرُ وَٱلۡمَيۡسِرُ وَٱلۡأَنصَابُ وَٱلۡأَزۡلَٰمُ رِجۡسٞ مِّنۡ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ فَٱجۡتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ ﴿90﴾ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ أَن يُوقِعَ بَيۡنَكُمُ ٱلۡعَدَٰوَةَ وَٱلۡبَغۡضَآءَ فِي ٱلۡخَمۡرِ وَٱلۡمَيۡسِرِ وَيَصُدَّكُمۡ عَن ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَعَنِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِۖ فَهَلۡ أَنتُم مُّنتَهُونَ ﴿91﴾

cards.title: Abolition of Pre-Islamic Zihar Divorce ('Like My Mother's Back') and Expiation
cards.note: Surah 58:1–4 addresses a woman disputing her husband's pre-Islamic zihar oath ('You are to me like my mother's back'), outlawing the Jahiliyyah divorce formula and mandating a three-tier expiation before marital resumption.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes recount that Khawlah bint Tha'labah complained to the Prophet after her husband Aws ibn al-Samit pronounced the pre-Islamic zihar oath, prompting revelation that replaced permanent separation with expiation.
discussion.reply: As al-Tabari documents on 58:2 from early authorities including Abu Qilabah, the formula 'You are to me like my mother's back' was a binding customary divorce oath in pre-Islamic Arabia. Rather than erasing the pagan oath's legal effect, Surah 58:3–4 recognizes the utterance as creating a binding marital prohibition that requires a tiered ritual expiation (kaffarah) to lift.

cards.quranEn: [1] God has heard the words of the woman who disputes with you about her husband, and (who) complains to God, and God hears the discussion of the two of you. Surely God is hearing, seeing. [2] Those of you who declare their wives to be as their mothers’ backs – they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave them birth. Surely they indeed say a wrong word and a falsehood. Yet surely God is indeed pardoning (and) forgiving. [3] Those who declare their wives to be as their mothers’ backs, (and) then return to what they have said, (the penalty is) the setting free of a slave before the two of them touch each other. That is what you are admonished. God is aware of what you do. [4] Whoever does not find (the means to do that), (the penalty is) a fast for two months consecutively, before the two of them touch each other. And whoever is not able (to do that), (the penalty is) the feeding of sixty poor persons. That is so that you may believe in God and His messenger. Those are the limits (set by) God – and for the disbelievers (there will be) a painful punishment.
quranHighlights: Those of you who declare their wives to be as their mothers’ backs – they are not their mothers
(the penalty is) the setting free of a slave before the two of them touch each other

sources.title: Tafsir al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan)
sources.en: He, whose mention is exalted, says: Those who make their wives unlawful to themselves with God's prohibition upon them of the backs of their mothers, so they say to them: 'You are to us like the backs of our mothers', and that was the divorce of a man (from) his wife during the Jahiliyyah. Thus Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, he said: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, he said: Zihar was a divorce during the Jahiliyyah, which if one of them spoke it, he could never return to his wife. So God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning it what He revealed.
highlights: 'You are to us like the backs of our mothers', and that was the divorce of a man (from) his wife during the Jahiliyyah
Zihar was a divorce during the Jahiliyyah, which if one of them spoke it, he could never return to his wife
sources.orig: يقول تعالى ذكره: الذين يحرّمون نساءهم على أنفسهم تحريم الله عليهم &; 23-228 &; ظهور أمهاتهم، فيقولون لهنّ: أنتن علينا كظهور أمهاتنا، وذلك كان طلاق الرجل امرأته في الجاهلية. كذلك حدثني يعقوب، قال: ثنا ابن علية، قال: ثنا أيوب، عن أبي قلابة، قال: كان الظهار طلاقا في الجاهلية، الذي إذا تكلم به أحدهم لم يرجع في امرأته أبدا، فأنـزل الله عزّ وجلّ فيه ما أنـزل.

cards.quranAr: قَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّتِي تُجَٰدِلُكَ فِي زَوۡجِهَا وَتَشۡتَكِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَسۡمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَآۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ ﴿1﴾ ٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِهِمۡۖ إِنۡ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡ إِلَّا ٱلَّـٰٓـِٔي وَلَدۡنَهُمۡۚ وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنكَرٗا مِّنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَزُورٗاۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٞ ﴿2﴾ وَٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِن نِّسَآئِهِمۡ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا قَالُواْ فَتَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةٖ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ تُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرٞ ﴿3﴾ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ شَهۡرَيۡنِ مُتَتَابِعَيۡنِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ فَإِطۡعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسۡكِينٗاۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۗ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ ﴿4﴾

cards.title: Pilgrimage (Hajj) to the House at Bakkah and the Station of Abraham
cards.note: Surah 3:96–97 mandates pilgrimage (Hajj) to the ancient sanctuary at Bakkah and its inviolable precinct, incorporating the pre-Islamic Meccan circumambulation rite attested in the sixth-century Mu'allaqah of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma.

discussion.view: Islamic tradition holds that Bakkah is an ancient name for Mecca where Abraham and Ishmael raised the first house of worship and left Abraham's footprint on the stone station (Maqam Ibrahim).
discussion.reply: Verse 17 of the pre-Islamic Mu'allaqah of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma (~AD 590) swears by 'the sacred edifice around which the men of Quraysh and Jurhum, who built it, make devout processions,' attesting before Islam that the Meccan shrine was venerated by Arab tribes as an ancient house of circumambulation and sanctuary truce.

cards.quranEn: [96] Surely the first House laid down for the people was indeed that at Becca, a blessed (House) and a guidance for the worlds. [97] In it are clear signs: the standing place of Abraham. Whoever enters it is secure. Pilgrimage to the House is (an obligation) on the people to God – (for) anyone who is able (to make) a way to it. Whoever disbelieves – surely God is wealthy beyond the worlds.
quranHighlights: Surely the first House laid down for the people was indeed that at Becca
Whoever enters it is secure. Pilgrimage to the House is (an obligation) on the people to God

sources.title: Mu'allaqah of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma
sources.ref: Mu'allaqah of Zuhayr, v. 17 (Pre-Islamic Circumambulation of the Ka'ba by Quraysh and Jurhum)
sources.workSub: Mu'allaqah of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma
sources.en: 17. I have sworn by the sacred edifice, round which the sons of Koraish and Jorham, who built it, make devout processions.
highlights: I have sworn by the sacred edifice, round which the sons of Koraish and Jorham, who built it, make devout processions.

cards.quranAr: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيۡتٖ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ مُبَارَكٗا وَهُدٗى لِّلۡعَٰلَمِينَ ﴿96﴾ فِيهِ ءَايَٰتُۢ بَيِّنَٰتٞ مَّقَامُ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۖ وَمَن دَخَلَهُۥ كَانَ ءَامِنٗاۗ وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ حِجُّ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ مَنِ ٱسۡتَطَاعَ إِلَيۡهِ سَبِيلٗاۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ ﴿97﴾

cards.title: Prescribed Fasting with Make-Up Days for Sickness or Travel
cards.note: Surah 2:183–185 prescribes fasting 'as it was prescribed for those before you' and allows the sick or travelers to make up missed days later, combining Numbers 9:10–11, Mishnah Yoma 8:5, and pre-Islamic 'Ashura fasting in Bukhari 4504.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes state that God prescribed fasting for earlier prophetic communities and transitioned the Muslim community from the earlier fast of 'Ashura to the month of Ramadan with merciful exemptions for illness and travel.
discussion.reply: Surah 2:183 explicitly appeals to the precedent of earlier communities ('as it was prescribed for those who were before you'). Its rule allowing a traveler to postpone the fast to an equal count of later days mirrors the Second Passover travel-postponement law of Numbers 9:10–11, combined with the illness exemption of Mishnah Yoma 8:5 and the pre-Islamic/Jewish 'Ashura fast in Sahih al-Bukhari 4504.

cards.quranEn: [183] You who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, as it was prescribed for those who were before you, so that you may guard (yourselves). [184] (Fast for) a number of days. Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days. And for those who can afford it, (there is) a ransom: feeding a poor person. Whoever does good voluntarily – it is better for him. But to fast is better for you, if (only) you knew. [185] The month of Ramaḍān, in which the Qur’ān was sent down as a guidance for the people, and as clear signs of the guidance and the Deliverance: so whoever of you is present during the month, let him fast in it, but whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days. God wishes to make it easy for you, and does not wish any hardship for you. And (He wishes) that you should fulfill the number (of days), and that you should magnify God for having guided you, and that you should be thankful.
quranHighlights: Fasting is prescribed for you, as it was prescribed for those who were before you
Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days

sources.title: Book of Numbers (LXX / Torah)
sources.en: Speak to the children of Israel, saying, Whatever man shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or on a journey far off, among you, or among your posterity; he shall then keep the passover to the Lord, in the second month, on the fourteenth day; in the evening they shall offer it, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs shall they eat it.
highlights: Whatever man shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or on a journey far off
he shall then keep the passover to the Lord, in the second month

sources.title: Mishnah Yoma 8:5
sources.en: If a person is ill and requires food due to potential danger, one feeds him according to the advice of medical experts who determine that he indeed requires food. And if there are no experts there, one feeds him according to his own instructions, until he says that he has eaten enough and needs no more.
highlights: If a person is ill and requires food due to potential danger, one feeds him
sources.orig: עֻבָּרָה שֶׁהֵרִיחָה, מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתָהּ עַד שֶׁתָּשִׁיב נַפְשָׁהּ. חוֹלֶה מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ עַל פִּי בְקִיאִין. וְאִם אֵין שָׁם בְּקִיאִין, מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר דָּי:

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari (Pre-Islamic Quraysh Fasting on 'Ashura Before Ramadan)
sources.workSub: Sahih al-Bukhari (Pre-Islamic Quraysh Fasting on 'Ashura Before Ramadan)
sources.en: Narrated Aisha:During the Pre-Islamic Period of ignorance the Quraish used to observe fasting on the day of 'Ashura', and the Prophet (ﷺ) himself used to observe fasting on it too. But when he came to Medina, he fasted on that day and ordered the Muslims to fast on it.
highlights: During the Pre-Islamic Period of ignorance the Quraish used to observe fasting on the day of 'Ashura'
sources.orig: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى، حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي أَبِي، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ ـ رضى الله عنها ـ قَالَتْ كَانَ يَوْمُ عَاشُورَاءَ تَصُومُهُ قُرَيْشٌ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، وَكَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَصُومُهُ، فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ الْمَدِينَةَ صَامَهُ وَأَمَرَ بِصِيَامِهِ، فَلَمَّا نَزَلَ رَمَضَانُ كَانَ رَمَضَانُ الْفَرِيضَةَ، وَتُرِكَ عَاشُورَاءُ، فَكَانَ مَنْ شَاءَ صَامَهُ، وَمَنْ شَاءَ لَمْ يَصُمْهُ‏.‏

cards.quranAr: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ ﴿183﴾ أَيَّامٗا مَّعۡدُودَٰتٖۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٖ فَعِدَّةٞ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةٞ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينٖۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَهُوَ خَيۡرٞ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ ﴿184﴾ شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدٗى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٖ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٖ فَعِدَّةٞ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ ﴿185﴾
